content.title: Approve or reject a high-value enterprise order
content.description: A Procurement Manager reviews pending approval requests for orders above the spending threshold, sees the requester and total context, approves to place the order or rejects with a sufficiently detailed reason, is prevented from acting on their own request, and leaves an auditable decision record.
content.summary: Review and decide high-value order requests.
content.value: Enforces spending policy, segregation of duties, and auditability on high-value purchases.
criteria: Orders whose total, including tax and delivery, exceeds $25,000 require Procurement Manager approval.
Submitting for approval creates a request ID in the format `REQ-` followed by 5 digits and stores status `Pending Approval`, requester name, total, and submitted time.
The Approvals page lists all requests with their status, and pending requests expose `Approve` and `Reject` actions to approvers.
Rejecting a request requires a reason of at least 10 characters, changes the request status to `Rejected`, and shows the reason to the requester.
Approving a request changes its status to `Approved` and places the order, generating an order number.
An approver cannot approve or reject their own request; those actions are hidden and the message `You cannot approve your own request` is shown.
Every approval decision records approver, timestamp, and reason.
